A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same entropy–memorization and EMBEDI study, with comparable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. V2 Appendix E corresponds to v3 Appendix D. Although one prompt is visually clipped in v3, its embedded text remains extractable.

before.justification: V2 reports original memorization experiments, dataset-inference results, and supplementary analyses of sampling strategies, generation lengths, and semantic clusters.

after.justification: V3 retains the original memorization experiments, dataset-inference results, and supplementary analyses in Appendices C and D.

M1.justification: The instance-wise and level-set entropy estimators, LCS filtering, and EMBEDI thresholding procedures are unchanged. No algorithmic component is added or revised.

E1.justification: The same training corpora, LiveBench and MIMIR coverage, and semantic-cluster evaluations remain. Removing one illustrative configuration-file example does not establish a change in dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: No evaluated comparator is added or removed. The instance-wise entropy analysis used to motivate the level-set estimator and the dataset-inference comparisons remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Both versions retain the same models, sample counts, prompt and generation lengths, LCS filtering, edit-distance metric, and supplementary evaluation protocols. No stated experimental setting is revised.

E4.justification: V3 removes v2 Appendix D's gibberish-memorization case study, including the configuration-file prompt and OLMo-1B's exact SHA-512 continuation. The sampling, generation-length, semantic-cluster analyses, and LiveBench case study remain.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting practices are unchanged. There are no additions or removals of seed information, repeated-run counts, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The qualitative SHA-512 exact-reproduction result is removed. The retained LiveBench example loses its exact-match assertion, which conflicted with its existing two-distance description. Numerical entries in Tables 1–7 and the plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, entropy definitions, normalized-entropy derivation, and equations in Sections 2–5 are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or mathematical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and Section 9 retain the same claims about the entropy–memorization relationship, token-distribution properties, and dataset inference through EMBEDI.

C2.justification: Section 8.2 removes the credential-design implication that maximizing character-level entropy does not minimize leakage and that some credentials are easiest to memorize. The remaining interpretations and stated limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain unchanged, including four RTX 3090 GPUs, Ubuntu 22.04, vLLM, sampling instructions, and EMBEDI thresholds and minimum sample size. Code and data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 7 and the same 70 reference entries are retained. Bibliography reflow does not change cited works or research positioning.

P1.justification: V3 updates the author and affiliation block, removes email contacts and short passages, and renumbers the dataset-inference appendix from E to D. Most scientific prose and the main narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 15 and Table 7 are repositioned within the shortened appendix, retaining their designs. The LiveBench prompt changes from a wrapped, shaded listing to an unwrapped line extending beyond the right page edge, making much of it visually unreadable.

improvement.justification: V3 corrects the contradictory exact-match caption on the two-distance example and narrows the credential-related discussion. However, its reformatted LiveBench prompt is clipped at the page boundary, whereas v2 displayed it as a wrapped listing. This prevents normal inspection of the full example and produces a limited net decline in presentation quality; the central scientific evidence remains unchanged.
